source.citation: Discussion of a paper on morphine, Medical Record 48 (1895): 709. The speaker is not named in the excerpt; Dr. Walker closed the discussion. To confirm from the page image.

complaints: severe headache about once a month, for years
presentation.course: For years her physician relieved each attack with a single hypodermic injection of morphine.

treatments.treatment: single hypodermic injection of morphine at each attack

treatments.response: headaches ceased, and no more morphine was needed

outcome: Headaches ceased after the eye operation.
quotes: he was in the habit of giving her relief with a single hypodermic injection of morphine
from that time the headaches had ceased

modernReading.text: Migraine, probably menstrual. Many doctors then blamed headaches on eye-muscle imbalance and operated; the remission may be coincidence or expectation. Regular morphine for headache risks dependence and more frequent headaches.

fixed: relief only from morphine so far
free: whether she asks for the injection

notes: The doctor in the discussion admits it seemed cruel to refuse an injection that worked. A good test of whether the player keeps giving morphine.
